text:
jon: Heads up — seeing a cluster-wide uptick in Xid 13/31 after this morning's kernel+driver canary in us-west-2. Started ~08:12. :eyes:

maria: Which kernel/driver combo did the canary pick up? how many cards affected?

jon: Canary hosts: gw-west-22, gw-west-23, gw-west-27. Kernel=6.1.19, nvidia-driver=535.86.10. 3 hosts, 12 GPUs total. Error rate jumped from ~0.02% to ~0.8% of sessions. Quick log snippet:```
[08:12:43] NVRM: Xid (13): Unsupported function
[08:12:44] NVRM: GPU 0000:01:00.0: Attempted read from inaccessible page
[08:12:44] kernel: nvidia 0000:01:00.0: GPU panic
```

deploy-bot: canary-rollout: us-west-2/generic-gpu-6.1.19/535.86.10 -> completed (3 hosts) :info:

alex: hmm. Could be driver/kernel interaction with ECC handling. Any ECC-corrected counters rising? also are these preemptible instances?

jon: ECC corrected counters are climbing on gw-west-27. These are a mix — 2 preemptible, 1 reserved on each host. Preemptible churn might be masking some symptoms. Quick stats: ```
GPU 0 ECC_CORRECTED=124 -> 892 over 40m
GPU 1 ECC_CORRECTED=40 -> 410 over 40m
```

sre-oncall: before rolling anything back, let's reproduce with a controlled burn-in on a single host and capture kv-cache traces + dmesg. Run the stress loop and attach /var/log/nvidia-installer.log + dmesg tail. Use:```
for i in {1..200}; do ./stress-tokens --len 2048 || true; sleep 1; done
dmesg | grep -i nvrm -A3 | tail -n 50
```

jon: running now on gw-west-22. attaching a short trace pasted below — no full upload to threads to avoid logs explosion:```
08:37:10 NVRM: Xid (31): GPU access fault at pc 0x7f2e3c...
08:37:11 GPU panic dump size=4MB -> saved /var/crash/gpu-dump-22.bin
```

firmware-bot: detected firmware divergence: gw-west-23 has VBIOS 94.02.7 while gw-west-22/27 have 94.02.5. Recommend uniform firmware for canary. :warning:

ops-lead: We need a drain/replace plan if this is flaky HW. Current reserved capacity in us-west-2 is tight — draining 3 hosts would cut available GPU pool by ~18%. Cost to spin up spot replacements is ~+$1.2k/day. Can we short-circuit by pinning kernel to 6.0.x on canary only?

maria: Good call. Let's try a two-arm canary: revert kernel to 6.0.20 + driver 535.86.10 on gw-west-23 (firmware 94.02.7) and keep other two on 6.1.19. Collect 6h smoke/telemetry. If Xid drops on 6.0 host we have signal. Also collect pcie link flaps with `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` for throughput anomalies.

alex: I'll prepare a lightweight smoke image with explicit kv-cache telemetry and smaller token lengths to surface Xid quickly. Also schedule a burn-in job that exercises ECC heavy patterns.

jon: quick interim result after switching gw-west-23 to 6.0.20: Xid rate on that host normalized to ~0.03%, while the two 6.1 hosts remain high. Early sign points to kernel/driver interaction. Attached minimal dmesg diff:```
--- gw-west-23 (6.0.20)
+ NVRM: no new panic
--- gw-west-22 (6.1.19)
+ NVRM: Xid (13) 3x/min
```

sre-oncall: great repro signal. Next steps: 1) hold global rollout, 2) create a regression test that runs on every driver/kernel pairing in CI (matrix), 3) coordinate with driver vendor for potential regression, 4) schedule fleet firmware homogenization after root cause narrow.

ops-lead: Agree. For capacity: spin up 4 spot replacements in us-west-2 with older kernel image as temporary buffer to avoid customer impact. I'll approve up to $2k extra/day for 48h. Please tag tickets and include expected rollback window.

maria: I'll own the regression CI job and the telemetry guardrail: will add alert rule for Xid rate >0.2% sustained 10m to trigger auto-fallback to pinned kernel 6.0 on canary hosts.

jon: thanks all — rolling this into an incident PR with logs + reproducer. Plan: 24h controlled canary on mixed kernels, collect full kv-cache+dmesg, vendor triage if signal holds. Will post updates. :white_check_mark:
